govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ClassificationU: This FBI memorandum on Lee Harvey Oswald — October 22, 1964 — is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. The Bureau’s paper trail is vast. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DomesticIntelli: Dusko Doder’s Washington Post piece — Trudeau Confronts a ‘Watergate’ — covers the Canadian scandal. Scandals crossed borders in the 1970s. Trudeau’s government survived. The press had a field day. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
deductive-logic: St. George Stock's compact textbook introduces the classic art of deductive reasoning — syllogisms, propositions, and the rules of valid argument. Clear definitions and worked examples guide students through logic's traditional forms. Though newer methods have joined it, the book remains a lucid introduction to thinking straight.
by-pike-and-dyke-a-tale-of-the-rise-of-t: Henty returns to the Netherlands' struggle for freedom, following a young Englishman through the sieges and sea-fights of the Dutch revolt. Pike and dyke — war on land and water — fill this stirring tale of the rise of the Dutch Republic. History as adventure, Henty-style.
the-boy-aviators-polar-dash-or-facing-de: John Henry Goldfrap's boy aviators fly to the Antarctic in a polar dash full of ice, danger, and daring. Written in the heroic age of exploration, it thrilled young readers with the ultimate adventure. Early aviation meets the last continent.
tales-of-the-enchanted-islands-of-the-at: Thomas Wentworth Higginson gathers the legends of the enchanted Atlantic isles — Atlantis, Avalon, St. Brendan's isle, and more. Sailors' dreams and poets' fancies mingle in these charming tales. A delightful voyage through the mythology of the sea. Lost Atlantis, phantom saints, and isles of the blest drift through these dreamlike tales.
a-trip-to-scarborough-and-the-critic: Sheridan pairs his comedy A Trip to Scarborough with his immortal farce The Critic — the tale of Mr. Puff and his disastrous play. Two delights from the wittiest playwright of the age. Laughter, guaranteed. Town fops, Irish bluster, and Mr. Puff's theatrical disasters provide an evening of pure fun.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acrostic: This 1913 reference piece on the acrostic — the alphabetical psalms and Lamentations, verse by letter. Anthony Maas traces the Hebrew device. Sorrow spelled out from aleph to tau. Poetry's oldest form of order. The psalmist's art hid order in devotion. Scholars still admire the device.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andras-meduli: A 1913 entry on Andras Medulic — a name in the Balkan church story. Anthony Gancevic records what is known. The entry preserves his modest fame. The missions remember their workers. A laborer of the southern missions. His mission served the mountain villages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-syn: This 1913 reference article on the apostolic syndic — the Franciscans' lay agent. Gregory Cleary explains his needful office. The friars may own nothing. The syndic holds their goods. Poverty's legal friend. His appointment needs the bishop's leave. His office aids the mendicant rule.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-authentic: A 1913 entry on authentic in canon law — the genuine and the authoritative. Francis Albert explains its technical use. The Church sifts the true texts. The authentic voice binds the faithful. The law's stamp of genuineness. Its use is the canonists' daily bread.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-balderic: This 1913 reference piece on Balderic — a name in the church story. J. Vincent Crowne records what is known. The entry preserves his modest fame. The old registers keep his name. A figure of the ecclesiastical past. His feast graces the old calendars.
